matcher.description: The format version this file is written in.
Matcher id: bare in a registry file (`ruff`), `alias/id` once loaded. Equals its folder name.
With one output, the prompt text. With `outputs`, a one-line summary for people.
Named pattern pieces: `$NAME` in a template, `%{NAME}` in a regex.
The outputs, when there are several.
One output only: finds the anchor lines.
One output only: one spelling each.
One output only: lines kept around the anchor.

output.description: What the evidence means; prompt text. 20-250 printable ASCII.
Ranks the window under budget pressure and tells the model how to read it.
Finds the anchor lines. Set this or `variants`.
One spelling each. Set this or `match`.
Which lines around the anchor become evidence.

variant.description: Only when this spelling needs a different window.

window.description: Start at the nearest matching line above, looking `within` lines up.
End at the next matching line, inclusive.
Keep extending while the next line matches.
Lines from the anchor down, at most; required with `until` and `while`. 1-500.

block.description: Closes it, on the first match after `start`.
Closes it after this many lines if `end` never comes.

node.description: RE2, matched anywhere in the line. `%{NAME}` inserts a `define`.
The line as it looks in the log: `$NAME` inserts a `define`, `...` is anything, `$$` is a `$`, and everything else is literal text. Matched anywhere in the line.
The line matches at least one item.
The line sits inside such a block.
A matching line is among the `within` lines above.
